transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doctor, I came because I’ve been doing odd things at church. Like at the potluck, I’ll stand there holding the serving spoon up and just not move. Or I’ll fold the same stack of napkins over and over while people are waiting on me. It’s been worrying me.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind and are hard to get rid of?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I have the same thought going around and around like that. I haven’t really noticed it, anyway.
Do you feel like you have to perform these actions, like holding the serving spoon or folding the napkins, for some reason?

I don’t know that I feel I have to do it for a reason. I just find myself doing it. Like I’ll be standing there at church with the serving spoon up, not moving, or messing with the same napkins over and over while folks are waiting. It’s odd, and I don’t really know why I do it.
Do you feel anxious when you're doing these repetitive actions or when you try to stop yourself from doing them?

I’m not sure, doctor. I don’t really notice feeling anxious when it’s happening. It’s more like I just catch myself doing it, and then I feel a little confused or embarrassed, but I can’t say it feels like anxiety.
Do you feel like these actions, such as holding the spoon or folding napkins, are part of a routine or ritual that you need to complete?

No, I don’t think it’s like a routine I’m trying to finish. It’s more that I find myself doing odd things at church, like holding the serving spoon up and just standing there, or folding the same napkins again and again while people are waiting. I don’t really feel like there’s a ritual to it.
Do you have any other behaviors or thoughts that you feel are repetitive or uncontrollable outside of these incidents at church?

Not really outside of that, doctor. The main thing is what happens at church—standing there by the potluck table with the serving spoon held up, or folding the same napkins over and over while people are waiting. I can’t think of other repetitive thoughts or behaviors like that.
Do these incidents at church cause you significant distress or interfere with your daily life or relationships?

Yes, it does some. I’ve had to step back from choir and some of the church volunteering. I get mixed up with plans, or what I’m supposed to handle, and then people get uncomfortable or have to fix it after me. That’s upsetting, and it makes me feel like I shouldn’t be doing as much there.
Have you noticed any problems at work or in your relationships with friends and family because of these incidents at church?

I’m not working now, so I can’t say about a job. But with church people, yes, it has caused some trouble. I’ve had to step back from choir and volunteering because I mix up plans or what I’m supposed to do, and then people get uncomfortable or have to redo things after me. It’s embarrassing.
Have you felt like you're avoiding social situations outside of church because of these incidents?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed myself avoiding people outside of church because of it. I mostly just get uneasy about things at church.
Have you felt like your behavior at church has affected your relationships with family or friends who are not part of the church?

Not really with family or friends outside the church, no. It’s mostly been at church. I’ve had to step back from choir and some volunteering because I get plans mixed up, and then people there get uncomfortable or have to redo what I was supposed to do.
Have you felt like these incidents have affected your overall self-esteem or how you see yourself as a person?
I’m not really sure. I feel embarrassed sometimes when things go wrong at church, but I don’t know that it’s changed how I see myself as a person. I haven’t thought about it that way much.
Do you have any unwanted thoughts that keep coming back to you?
I’m not sure. I don’t really notice thoughts that keep coming back like that. Sometimes I think about what happened at church, but I don’t know if I’d call them unwanted thoughts.
Have you noticed any difficulty with daily tasks or responsibilities at home because of these incidents or behaviors?

At home, not so much. It’s more been at church. I’ve had to stop doing some choir and volunteer things because I get plans mixed up, and then people have to fix it or they get uncomfortable. But around the house, I don’t think it’s caused much trouble.
Have you noticed any problems in your daily life or relationships outside of church due to these incidents or behaviors?

Outside of church, I don’t think it’s been much of a problem. It’s mostly that I had to step back from choir and helping with church things because I mix up plans, and then people get uncomfortable or have to redo what I was supposed to do. Relationships otherwise, I haven’t really noticed much.
Do you think you've always been a bit like this, even before these incidents at church started happening?
No, I don’t think I was always like this. It seems like it started after my closest friend in the choir died… that was about 11 months ago now. Since then, things have just been different.
Did you notice these behaviors at church starting right after your friend died, or was there some time in between?

There was some time in between. After she died, I was grieving, but the really odd things at church, and me talking in a way people couldn’t follow sometimes… I’d say that’s been more like the last 6 months.
Have you generally felt like you don't quite fit in with the people around you, even before these incidents at church started?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve always been a little quiet maybe, but I didn’t feel like I didn’t fit in before all this. I got along with people well enough.
Do you have any thoughts that you try to ignore or suppress, but they keep coming back to you?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get worries like anybody, but I haven’t noticed thoughts that keep coming back no matter how much I try to push them away.
Do you think these behaviors at church are somehow connected to your friend's death?
Yes, I think so. It seems like the change started after my closest choir friend died… that was about 11 months ago. I can’t say exactly how, but it feels connected.
Do you feel like the way you do things at church needs to be perfect or exactly right?
I’m not sure. I don’t really think of it as needing to be perfect. I just do what I do, I guess. I haven’t noticed myself worrying about it being exactly right.
